purpose: v3.6's sign gate with tanh squash removed — linear probe contribution keeps the gate's full strength on confident rows
probe_weights: submission/whitebox_probe (shared trunk, all 3 families, balanced recipe)

selection.method: sweep linear vs tanh across caps 2-20, sign gate kept, Iris edge +0.068, Notus probe at 0.5586 and 0.48 inverted
selection.iris_regime: judge blunted to probe_auroc - 0.068 (real Iris condition)
selection.notus_regime: probe blunted to measured 0.5586 (and 0.48 inverted), judge healthy
selection.why_linear: the tanh compresses probe_z above ~2, holding back the most confident rows on Iris where the probe is strong (0.9918 AUROC). Removing it lets those rows contribute at full strength.
selection.why_12_not_8: linear cap8 already matches v3.6 tanh cap12's gain, but it does so on different rows (slightly higher Iris, slightly lower Notus). Cap12 adds a clean +0.0010 on top for no measurable cost.

selection_notes.notus_blind_spot: the local Notus proxy has the judge at 0.938 against real Notus's ~0.864 — same as v3.6
selection_notes.iris_capture_anomaly: part of the Iris shortfall remains unexplained — same as v3.6
selection_notes.probe_in_sample_caveat: the probe is in-sample on every dev fold — same as v3.6
selection_notes.extreme_disagreement_risk: without tanh, a 5-sigma probe on a disagreement row contributes 0.208×5=1.04 judge-z units (vs 0.208 with tanh), which can flip a borderline (±1σ) judge. The measured cost on aggregate Notus is -0.0002, same as with tanh, because 5σ events are too rare to register. This is a principled cost of removing the squash.
